questions.text:
In the Newton-Raphson method, an initial guess of [latex]x_{0}=2[/latex] is made and the sequence [latex]x_{0},x_{1},x_{2}...[/latex] is obtained for the function
[latex]0.75x^{3}-2x^{2}-2x+4=0[/latex]
Consider the statements
(I) [latex]x_{3}[/latex]=0.
(II) The method converges to a solution in a finite number of iterations.
Which of the following is TRUE?
questions.solution:
[latex]f(x)=0.75x^3-2x^2-2x+4,\quad f'(x)=2.25x^2-4x-2[/latex]

- [latex]x_0=2[/latex]: f = [latex]-[/latex]2, f' = [latex]-[/latex]1 [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] [latex]x_1=2-\frac{-2}{-1}=0[/latex]
- [latex]x_1=0[/latex]: f = 4, f' = [latex]-[/latex]2 [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] [latex]x_2=0-\frac{4}{-2}=2[/latex]

The values repeat 2, 0, 2, 0, ... so [latex]x_3=0[/latex] (I true), and the method never converges (II false).

Answer: Only I

questions.text: A non-zero polynomial f(x) of degree 3 has roots at x = 1,x = 2 and x = 3. Which one of the following must be TRUE?
questions.solution:
[latex]f(x)=c(x-1)(x-2)(x-3)[/latex] with [latex]c\ne0[/latex].

[latex]f(0)=-6c,\quad f(4)=6c[/latex]
[latex]f(0)f(4)=-36c^2\lt 0[/latex] always (whatever the sign of c), while the sum f(0) + f(4) = 0.

Answer: [latex]f(0)f(4)\lt 0[/latex]

questions.text:
If the matrix A is such that
[latex]\begin{bmatrix} 2\\ -4\\ 7 \end{bmatrix}\begin{bmatrix} 1 &9 &5 \end{bmatrix}[/latex]
Then the determinant of A is equal to ________.
questions.solution:
A is a column vector times a row vector, so every row of A is a multiple of [1 9 5]. Hence rank(A) = 1.

A 3 [latex]\times[/latex] 3 matrix with rank 1 is singular, so det(A) = 0.

Answer: 0

questions.text:
A function f(x) is continuous in the interval [0,2]. It is known that f(0)=f(2)=-1 and f(1)=1.
Which one of the following statements must be true?
questions.solution:
Let g(y) = f(y) [latex]-[/latex] f(y + 1) on [0, 1]. g(0) = f(0) [latex]-[/latex] f(1) = [latex]-[/latex]2 and g(1) = f(1) [latex]-[/latex] f(2) = 2. g is continuous and changes sign, so g(y) = 0 for some y in (0, 1), i.e. f(y) = f(y + 1).

Answer: There exists a y in (0,1) such that f(y)=f(y+1)

options: There exists a y in the interval (0,1) such that f(y)=f(y+1)
For every y in the interval (0,1), f(y)=f(2-y)
The maximum value of the function in the interval (0.2) is 1
There exists a y in the interval (0,1) such that f(y)=-f(2-y)

questions.text: The function [latex]f(x)=x sin x[/latex] satisfies the following equation: [latex]f''(x)+f(x)+tcos x=0[/latex]. The value of t is______.
questions.solution:
[latex]f'=\sin x+x\cos x[/latex], [latex]f''=2\cos x-x\sin x[/latex].
[latex]f''+f=2\cos x[/latex], so [latex]2\cos x+t\cos x=0\Rightarrow t=-2[/latex].

Answer: -2
